newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Dead man's son joins calls for NZ pit bull ban.
newsitem.headline: Dead man's son joins calls for NZ pit bull ban.

text.p: The son of a New Zealand man savaged to death by a pit bull terrier joined calls on Tuesday for the dogs to be banned in New Zealand.

Kapi Dinsdale's father, Koro Maruki Dinsdale, a 59-year-old freezer plant worker, was killed on Sunday night in a frenzied attack by a pit bull terrier cross at his farm near the North Island town of Te Puke.
"The damage it did to him was unbelieveable; I couldn't look at it," Kapi Dinsdale told reporters.
"Those dogs are killers...My father was a fit, strong man and it just tore him to bits."
Police believe Dinsdale tried to break up a fight between the two dogs he had with him, and was himself attacked.

The Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) director Bob Kerridge said the SPCA had pleaded with the government 10 years ago not to allow pit bull terriers into the country, but was told owners and not the dogs were the problem.
Kerridge disagreed, saying, "The pit bull is the one breed of dog which we say you cannot control, it is unpredictable, it is bred to kill and it is going to do its job."
The SPCA would renew its earlier call for a ban, he added, as under recently-introduced dog control laws the government has the power to ban dangerous dogs. It has not yet been used.
Local Government Minister Christine Fletcher told national newspapers the main difficulty was establishing which dogs should be banned because a large number were cross-breeds.
"We need to have a practical response. I will be working with my department to explore ways in which the dog numbers can be reduced. Something has to happen," she said.

Brisbane City Council recently became the first administration in Australia to ban the breeding of pit bull terriers while Britain has banned the import of pit bull types of dogs and their purchase, sale or exchange.
